title: Mild Kung Pao Wok Sauce
description: Two vinegars, toasted peanut and a trace of chile give this mild kung pao sauce its sweet, sour and nutty finish.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: For a plain infusion, steep sliced mushrooms in hot water, strain and add no salt. Estimate assumes 15 mg sodium per cup.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: ground ancho chile
ingredients.note: Use pure mild ancho, without added salt.

ingredients.name: finely ground Sichuan peppercorn husks
ingredients.note: Use a fine seedless grind for a gentle citrus aroma.

steps.title: Whisk the nut base
steps.text: Whisk {peanut}, {mu}, {a}, {rv}, {bv} and {bs} in a jug until smooth.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Warm {so} over medium-low heat in the HexClad and stir {ga}, {gi}, {an} and {sz} for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Whisk in the nut mixture and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes. The two vinegars give a rounded tang even without Chinese black vinegar.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Toss with moist chicken or spoon over shrimp. Serve extra chile separately so both plates stay mild.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit both peppers and use half of each vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 66 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 8.3 g total carbohydrate, 3.2 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 118 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 61 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 6.9 g total carbohydrate, 3.2 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 28 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
